crop.name: Winter squash (Cucurbita, kabocha/buttercup-type dark green squash — most consistent with Cucurbita maxima)
crop.distinguishing_features: One large sprawling vine dominating the frame: very broad shield-to-triangular lobed leaves with finely toothed/wavy margins, pale raised palmate-reticulate venation, and a dense short bristly pubescence that catches the light as a silvery stipple; thick, ribbed, hollow-looking succulent petioles and runners covered in stiff hairs; coiled branching tendrils at the nodes; and, decisively, fruit — a round ribbed fruit with very dark blue-green skin, pale green longitudinal stripes and fine white speckling resting on the straw, plus a young golf-ball-sized striped fruit still attached at a node with the shriveled brown blossom remnant on its tip.

weeds.name: Grasses (mixed; broader-bladed volunteer cereal/rye or barnyard-type grass plus finer bunch grass)
weeds.distinguishing_features: Narrow strap-like blades with strictly parallel venation and no net reticulation, smooth and hairless with a waxy blue-green to bright yellow-green cast, rising in stiff arcs and fans from the straw rather than from a thick petiole; they cross in front of and behind the squash leaves everywhere and have no lobes, teeth, tendrils or hairs. Clearly a different growth form from the crop.

weeds.name: Purslane-like fleshy-leaved seedling (Portulaca oleracea type)
weeds.distinguishing_features: Low sprawling seedling on the bare straw away from the vine: small, thick, smooth, hairless spoon/paddle-shaped leaves with entire margins arranged in whorled clusters at the ends of short succulent reddish-tinged stems; glossy and untoothed, in sharp contrast to the crop's huge dull-hairy toothed leaves.

weeds.name: Small round scallop-leaved broadleaf seedlings (mallow / henbit-or-ground-ivy type)
weeds.distinguishing_features: Tiny rosettes and creeping stems in the mulch: nearly circular to kidney-shaped leaves an inch or less across with rounded, crenate (scalloped) margins, palmate venation and a soft hairy surface, borne on slender thread-like petioles. Same leaf outline family as a squash cotyledon-stage plant but far too small, with no bristly stem, no tendrils, and no attachment to the vine.

weeds.name: Clover-type trifoliate seedling
weeds.distinguishing_features: A few small three-parted leaflets with rounded tips and finely toothed edges on thin stems at the edge of the straw — trifoliate arrangement never occurs on the squash.

non_plant_material: Dry straw / cut-stalk mulch covering most of the ground
Bare dry soil and small clods showing through the mulch
Weathered dead stem and twig fragments, including a dark rotted woody piece
A small pale gray-white feather lying on the straw
Dried brown withered squash blossom remnant still attached at the tip of the young fruit (dead plant tissue, not a living plant)
Small light-colored grit/pebble-like specks and pale insect-egg-like flecks on the mulch
